engine_status.note: Customer prod box should also show active_engine=v3. If it shows heuristic, there is a deployment problem, not an algorithm problem.

framework_symmetry_check.setup: heuristic vs heuristic, 500 games, seed=1, max_turns=150

heuristic_vs_random.setup: heuristic vs random, 500 games, seed=1, max_turns=150

v3_baseline_unchanged_params.setup: orchestrator:v3 vs heuristic, 500 games, seed=1, params=shipped/V2
v3_baseline_unchanged_params.conclusion: V3 engine with A-0+A-1+A-2a C++ code and SHIPPED V2 params already beats heuristic by 28.8 points. A-1 (exact shanten + chance-node fix) is the single biggest contributor.

v3_with_retrained_sklearn_params.setup: orchestrator:v3 vs heuristic, 500 games, seed=1, params=freshly trained from 2000 selfplay games
v3_with_retrained_sklearn_params.conclusion: Retraining with the new 114-feature sklearn path on fresh data adds another 3.8 win rate points and drops houjuu rate from 15.0% to 13.4%.

neural_vs_heuristic.setup: NeuralPolicy(MLP hidden=128, 20 epochs, 50k samples) vs heuristic, 200 games, seed=1
neural_vs_heuristic.conclusion: Offline metrics far better than sklearn (agari 0.849 vs 0.685, houjuu 0.848 vs 0.750) but winrate worse -- classic distribution shift: NN trained on heuristic-vs-heuristic data has under-calibrated houjuu prior. Fix is B-2b: iterative self-play retraining or C++ search-augmented inference.

ryukyoku_prob.note: all zeros in 2000-game sample; need ryukyoku-heavy dataset
